targets.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer.
targets.name: War Pigs

targets.approach: Start from the northern parking area; the trail passes beneath the Incinerator Wall and leads straight to the narrow, shady north face. The route is between Baku and Miner's Milk; look for the unusual wave-shaped crack above a big flake-like boulder at the base.
targets.name: Finger Crack

targets.approach: Start from the northern parking area; the trail passes beneath the Incinerator Wall and leads straight to the narrow, shady north face. It shares a start with Fun Police but stays in the gully to its right, passing a chockstone and a short chimney.
targets.name: Helmet Jammer

targets.approach: Start from the northern parking area; the trail passes beneath the Incinerator Wall and leads straight to the narrow, shady north face. It starts as for Boom Sauce; look for the squeeze tunnel that the flared crack leads to.
targets.name: The Blast Hole

targets.approach: Park short of the seasonal gate and walk up the paved road to the point level with Gate Rock, then push through the brush to the boulder. The route is on the northeast side of the boulder, overhanging at the start and easing to slab at the top.
targets.name: Gate Crack

targets.approach: Park short of the seasonal gate and walk up the paved road to the point level with Gate Rock, then push through the brush to the boulder. The route is on the southwest side of the boulder and is the easiest way to the top.
targets.descent_text: It is also the downclimb for the boulder.
targets.name: Pepper Crack

targets.approach: Neanderthal Wall is the pyramid-shaped granite wall seen to the northeast on the drive north into Kernville. It needs a rugged hike, either from Chimney Peak Road on the north or from Fay Ranch on the south. The route starts a good way left of Cro-Magnon Man, up a crack that lies just right of a left-facing corner, then traverses right to a vertical crack system, water groove and chimney to the top.
targets.name: Alley-Oop

targets.approach: Neanderthal Wall is the pyramid-shaped granite wall seen to the northeast on the drive north into Kernville. It needs a rugged hike, either from Chimney Peak Road on the north or from Fay Ranch on the south. The route follows the crack system that forms the longest continuous line from the foot of the pyramid to its summit.
targets.name: Cro-Magnon Man

targets.approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. The route is the third crack from the left on the north face, reached from the ledges below the corner.
targets.descent_text: From the ridge at the top, scramble off to climber's left.
targets.name: Abyssus Abyssum Invocat

targets.approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. Start at the base of the steep, right-leaning crack and corner system whose top is some way below a short, prominent offwidth.
targets.name: Grendel

targets.approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. Start at the thin crack running up the right edge of a tall flake, far beneath a vegetated offwidth.
targets.name: Marmot Fur Slippers

targets.approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. Start at a crack slanting right through white rock, under three roofs stacked one above another at the right of a crack-and-corner system.
targets.descent_text: Head left to the ridge from the top of the corner and scramble down to climber's left.
targets.name: Marmotzilla

targets.approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. It is the second crack from the left, at the left end of the face; reach it by traversing in from the left, or by one of several easy-angled routes up from the ledge system strewn with boulders.
targets.descent_text: Walk down to climber's left, or continue up the northeast ridge.
targets.name: My Own Worst Enemy

targets.approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. Start below a crack just left of the short pillars and flakes, which are just left of the giant chasm or chimney.
targets.descent_text: The route reaches the northeast ridge; one finish traverses left to the ridge, from where parties scramble off to climber's left.
targets.name: Nazgûl

targets.approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. The route follows a prominent crack system near the centre of the face.
targets.name: North face

targets.approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. It is the leftmost crack on the north face; get to it by traversing in from the left, or by one of several easy-angled lines up from the boulder-strewn ledges.
targets.descent_text: Walk down to climber's left, or continue up the northeast ridge.
targets.name: Public Enemy Number One

targets.approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. Scramble to the alcove beneath the rightmost wide crack, which is in the right-hand face of the large left-facing corner system on the right side of the face.
targets.descent_text: From the summit plateau, wander southeast across it and descend the talus and slabs of the northeast face.
targets.name: Sauron's Sport Route

targets.approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. Start on a ledge that a small chasm separates from the main wall, a short way below and left of a small pine; the line goes up the centre of the face.
targets.descent_text: From the plateau, hike southeast and drop down the second- and third-class talus and slabs of the northeast face.
targets.name: Shelob

targets.approach: Take forest road 2N13 to 2N13D, park at the intersection, and use the climbers path that climbs the ramp over the gully to Big Mama. The Lower Tier is the first side you see from the road, and a trail leads straight to it. The route is a diagonal crack inside the corridor on the lower north face.
targets.name: Yo-mama

targets.approach: Take forest road 2N13 to 2N13D, park at the intersection, and use the climbers path that climbs the ramp over the gully to Big Mama. For the Upper Tier, reach it with a scramble from the lower northwest side, or by walking round from the uphill back of the pinnacle. The route is a wide crack to the left of the bolted face.
targets.name: Get the Ball Rolling

targets.approach: Take forest road 2N13 to 2N13D, park at the intersection, and use the climbers path that climbs the ramp over the gully to Big Mama. For the Upper Tier, reach it with a scramble from the lower northwest side, or by walking round from the uphill back of the pinnacle. It shares the start of Queensryche, then goes left at the undercling and clips the three bolts up the left half of the face.
targets.name: Queens Left

targets.approach: Take forest road 2N13 to 2N13D, park at the intersection, and use the climbers path that climbs the ramp over the gully to Big Mama. For the Upper Tier, reach it with a scramble from the lower northwest side, or by walking round from the uphill back of the pinnacle. It is just right of Queens Left, a thin crack to an overlap, then the face above.
targets.name: Queensryche

targets.approach: Park at the Cliff Lake trailhead and follow the Cliff Lake trail to the lake. From there head east toward Bullfrog Lake and then to the base of Dogtooth Peak; depending on the time of year there may be river crossings. Traverse along the east face to the towers of exfoliating granite slabs on the southeast face, where a lightly used trail runs along the base, and watch for loose rock. The route starts directly left of the Lookout route, up a third and fourth class scramble from the big dead pine to the ledge with the first bolt.
targets.descent_text: Scramble the last bit to the summit, then take the hiking trail down the northern side of the peak, which serves as the walk-off.
targets.name: Gin and Juice

targets.approach: The crag is on the reservoir shore and is easiest by boat or kayak from the launch, which has day parking; it can also be reached on foot from near the dam. The route is at the crag's north end, beside a class 4 gully, and starts from a good ledge up a thin to mid-width crack.
targets.name: Fingers and Blades

targets.approach: From the small dirt pull-in beside the road, just before it runs under the face, walk north to a low ridge that rises west toward the bluff. Keep going to a very large black oak, then contour left through the woods around to the base of the wall. The old trail from the days of route development has grown over, so expect to find the way by eye. Antithesis begins under a slender, left-rising roof; Innervisions and Right-A-This begin next to it.
targets.name: Antithesis

targets.approach: From the small dirt pull-in beside the road, just before it runs under the face, walk north to a low ridge that rises west toward the bluff. Keep going to a very large black oak, then contour left through the woods around to the base of the wall. The old trail from the days of route development has grown over, so expect to find the way by eye. Blackbird begins at the left-hand end of the main wall in an easy-angled right-facing corner, then wanders upward.
targets.name: Blackbird

targets.approach: From the small dirt pull-in beside the road, just before it runs under the face, walk north to a low ridge that rises west toward the bluff. Keep going to a very large black oak, then contour left through the woods around to the base of the wall. The old trail from the days of route development has grown over, so expect to find the way by eye. This is a bolted line on the face, with a separate bolted route running parallel just to its right.
targets.name: E.C. Come, E.C. Go

targets.approach: From the small dirt pull-in beside the road, just before it runs under the face, walk north to a low ridge that rises west toward the bluff. Keep going to a very large black oak, then contour left through the woods around to the base of the wall. The old trail from the days of route development has grown over, so expect to find the way by eye. Entasis follows a line of bolts on the face just left of the big arch that Jaws climbs.
targets.name: Entasis

targets.approach: From the small dirt pull-in beside the road, just before it runs under the face, walk north to a low ridge that rises west toward the bluff. Keep going to a very large black oak, then contour left through the woods around to the base of the wall. The old trail from the days of route development has grown over, so expect to find the way by eye. Go Ask Alice is a short bolted line to the left of the long right-facing corner of White Rabbit.
targets.descent_text: A bolted anchor at the top of the route serves as the belay and the rappel station.
targets.name: Go Ask Alice

targets.approach: From the small dirt pull-in beside the road, just before it runs under the face, walk north to a low ridge that rises west toward the bluff. Keep going to a very large black oak, then contour left through the woods around to the base of the wall. The old trail from the days of route development has grown over, so expect to find the way by eye. Headache lies a long way over to the right of the main face, at a big whale-shaped pillar; it climbs the flared chimney that faces left along the pillar's left flank.
targets.name: Headache

targets.approach: From the small dirt pull-in beside the road, just before it runs under the face, walk north to a low ridge that rises west toward the bluff. Keep going to a very large black oak, then contour left through the woods around to the base of the wall. The old trail from the days of route development has grown over, so expect to find the way by eye. Inland Seafood climbs the bolted face on the right side of the Jaws arch.
targets.name: Inland Seafood

targets.approach: From the small dirt pull-in beside the road, just before it runs under the face, walk north to a low ridge that rises west toward the bluff. Keep going to a very large black oak, then contour left through the woods around to the base of the wall. The old trail from the days of route development has grown over, so expect to find the way by eye. Innervisions starts just right of Antithesis and goes up face climbing past a thin left-facing corner.
targets.name: Innervisions

targets.approach: From the small dirt pull-in beside the road, just before it runs under the face, walk north to a low ridge that rises west toward the bluff. Keep going to a very large black oak, then contour left through the woods around to the base of the wall. The old trail from the days of route development has grown over, so expect to find the way by eye. Jaws is the big arch on the face, a short flared chimney that widens to an offwidth.
targets.descent_text: A bolted anchor sits above the top of the arch. Rappel from it, or carry on up easy ground to the top.
targets.name: Jaws

targets.approach: From the small dirt pull-in beside the road, just before it runs under the face, walk north to a low ridge that rises west toward the bluff. Keep going to a very large black oak, then contour left through the woods around to the base of the wall. The old trail from the days of route development has grown over, so expect to find the way by eye. King of Pain begins on a ramp rising rightward, just right of the pedestal at the start of Ukiah.
targets.name: King of Pain

targets.approach: From the small dirt pull-in beside the road, just before it runs under the face, walk north to a low ridge that rises west toward the bluff. Keep going to a very large black oak, then contour left through the woods around to the base of the wall. The old trail from the days of route development has grown over, so expect to find the way by eye. Mr Parker's Parrot is the flared chimney up the pillar's right flank, the pillar that stands well away to the right of the main face.
targets.name: Mr Parker's Parrot

targets.approach: From the small dirt pull-in beside the road, just before it runs under the face, walk north to a low ridge that rises west toward the bluff. Keep going to a very large black oak, then contour left through the woods around to the base of the wall. The old trail from the days of route development has grown over, so expect to find the way by eye. Mystery Arete is a bolted direct start to Whaleback Crack, climbing the spine of the pillar.
targets.name: Mystery Arete
